newsitem.title: UK: Enel cancels Nigeria liguified natural gas contract.
newsitem.headline: Enel cancels Nigeria liguified natural gas contract.

text.p: Italian state power utility Enel has cancelled a long-term contract to buy Nigerian Liquified Natural Gas (LNG), the company said in a statement.

Enel said the decision to break the contract was linked to its abandonment of a project to construct a gas plant at Montalto di Castro, north of Rome, for economic, technical and environmental reasons.

"Following media reports concerning the decision to break the Nigerian LNG contract Enel would like to clarify that the reason for the force majeur stems from the decision to cancel a project for the construction for a gas plant in Montalto di Castro, due to lack of economic incentives," Enel said in a statement.
Enel signed the long-term contract in November and were to receive the first cargo of Nigerian LNG in the third quarter of 1999.
Nigeria's $4 billion LNG project plans to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of LNG per year from a plant projected to start production in 1999.
Partners in the project are the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, Shell Gas BV, Elf Aquitaine and Italy's Agip SpA.
Long-term supply contracts have been signed with Enargas of Spain and Gaz de France.
